hypotheses.statement: For a direct resource request, the retail opener prefers a loose file at the requested path and falls back to Data.sma when the loose CreateFileA open fails; virtual-root registration order may affect ambiguous archive matches.
evidence_for: Retail 0064D530 calls CreateFileA before archive fallback.
Fallback normalizes separators and matches DataAudio/DataGx/DataGame/DataScene/DataVideo roots.
evidence_against: Per-root search precedence and duplicate archive-name resolution were not reconstructed.
hypotheses.confidence_detail: Direct loose-first/fallback order is confirmed; multi-root and duplicate-entry precedence remain only medium confidence.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Inspect a breakpoint trace at 0064D530 for one resource existing both loose and packaged in a disposable retail install.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Trace 0064D530 branches, archive index lookup, root matching and duplicate-name selection; compare exact same paths in 9.10.0.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: Use cloned Data.sma and cloned game root with distinct sentinel payloads at one existing test path; record which payload is read, then restore the clone from hash-verified baseline.

hypotheses.statement: DataGame/DataScene Value elements are loaded into the common 0x1c-byte broker-entry representation, with Type and save flags controlling typed access and persistence participation.
evidence_for: Retail XML corpus uses Value Name/Type/Value and SaveOptions/SavePlayerState attributes.
Retail broker diagnostic dumps 0x1c entries, type, revision, scope, and save-flag bits.
Runtime wrappers use shared typed broker read/write helpers.
evidence_against: Exact XML-to-entry parser calls and merge order for all config families were not followed in this pass.
hypotheses.confidence_detail: The entry/access correlation is strong; the exact generic XML parser-to-entry merge path is not yet followed end-to-end.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Use the existing static parser path and one Value record to trace XML attributes into broker entry fields.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Decompile the generic XML node visitor and compare Type dispatch with the entry dump/type accessors; add cross-build map for parser core.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: On a disposable profile, change one non-critical broker-backed option and observe the parsed value and matching broker entry in debugger.

hypotheses.statement: SavePlayerState flags select broker values for player-state serialization, while SaveOptions selects settings serialization.
evidence_for: Progress.xml records are SavePlayerState=True and SaveOptions=False.
Broker dump prints save-related flag bits.
Progress wrappers set/get keys used by unlock and best-time systems.
evidence_against: The actual player save writer, file name/container, and serialization policy were not identified; flag names may be consumed by more than one persistence path.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Trace every retail reader of broker flag bit 0x1/0x2 and identify writer call sites before a runtime save diff.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Xref the diagnostic flag reads and broker serialization/dirty-state routines; identify a single SavePlayerState entry end-to-end.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: With the game closed and profile backed up, change one known progress field through normal play and compare only generated save files; restore the full profile copy.

hypotheses.statement: The retail BuildData wrapper is registered as an editor/development command and may be reachable through an in-game editor surface without executable patching.
evidence_for: Retail-only BuildData strings, wrapper, recursive walker and callback-like method-pointer table reference exist.
Neighboring editor and XML open/save functionality survives in retail.
evidence_against: The table owner and UI/dispatcher call chain have not been identified; data-pointer references do not prove menu visibility.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Trace the data table at 00692F8C to its owning class and list/command dispatch without running the command.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Resolve all reads of 00692F8C, its adjacent vtable/callback table, constructors, and editor menu population.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: On a disposable retail installation, check editor menus; invoke only if an ordinary UI command exists, and direct it at a copied test folder with output hashes recorded.

hypotheses.statement: Race/RecordReplay and Race/CarN/RecordSpline feed a recording path structurally related to the implemented GhostPlayback/GhostCar consumer.
evidence_for: RecordReplay and RecordSpline broker paths survive in all builds.
Retail GhostPlayback reads a start position and constructs a GhostCar.
evidence_against: No producer-to-file path, extension, or shared data structure was mapped; names alone may represent separate systems.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Trace the string xrefs/callers for RecordReplay and RecordSpline, then compare their data references with GhostCar playback.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Map recording enable path, file APIs, record structure, and ghost playback parser; identify runtime file extension.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: On a cloned profile, run one short race with recording enabled through an existing UI/config route; inventory only newly created files and restore the clone.

hypotheses.statement: LastMarker, SplitPoint, WrongWay, and pace-note owner/current-note broker keys participate in per-car route state, but their exact producers and transitions may be distributed across AI and race managers.
evidence_for: Formatted Race/Car%d/... keys exist across later builds.
RaceLine, split-time and pace-note component factories/configuration exist.
Existing R5T-D1 confirms a per-car SplitTime0 activation path, but not these other fields.
evidence_against: Several formatted strings have no direct xref; no marker progression or WrongWay detector was decompiled.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Search broker path construction at runtime/static call sites and identify whether these values are read or written in active race code.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Trace RaceLine/marker update call graph, string-construction helpers, and all broker read/write calls around the route classes.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: Watch broker access for Race/Car0/LastMarker and WrongWay in a cloned retail profile across one marker, reverse travel and a deliberate route departure; no course data edits in the active R5T experiment.

hypotheses.statement: The UDP listener on port 22222 serves a race synchronization or peer-discovery role, with network car slots potentially represented by indices 0 through 7.
evidence_for: All four builds bind configured port 0x56CE when the listener is enabled.
Network/SyncState and Network/CarN/IpAddress keys exist; race network-sync enforcer path is present.
evidence_against: Protocol and slot capacity are unknown; visible path suffixes do not establish an active maximum.
hypotheses.confidence_detail: Sync relation is plausible from keys and enforcer; eight-slot capacity is low confidence and unproven.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Trace all reads/writes of Network/SyncState and UDP send/receive call sites before any network experiment.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Map socket bind/recv/send call graph and inspect loop bounds on indexed network car records.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: Only on two isolated local copies, observe loopback socket state and broker changes; keep the listener offline from external peers and stop immediately if it attempts external endpoints.

hypotheses.statement: The explicit alpha-test shader families added by 9.10.0 distinguish binary/cutout alpha materials from blended alpha materials, while environment families add a separate stage/state path.
evidence_for: New alpha-test shader family names appear with the 9.3-to-9.10 registry rewrite.
Existing R4D.1 material findings distinguish alpha and environment states.
evidence_against: No per-material runtime selector branch was traced from a retail DX material value to an exact D3D render-state combination in this phase.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification_test: Trace one material with fractional alpha and one cutout material through retail selector 00580360 and inspect assembly/render-state calls.
hypotheses.static_follow_up: Pair selector and render-state functions with corresponding registry entries; inspect the values loaded at the D3D8 call boundary.
hypotheses.runtime_follow_up: Render two existing assets that differ only in known alpha semantics in an isolated retail install and capture device-state breakpoints; do not modify shared preview semantics from this result alone.
